questions.q: Why does this Power BI model use Import mode instead of DirectQuery?
options: DirectQuery is not supported for SQL Server connections
This is an operational dashboard Executives click through live in a meeting, and Import mode's in-memory engine keeps that interaction fast
Import mode is required whenever a model has more than one dimension
DirectQuery would let Power BI write back into the warehouse
questions.explain: Import mode loads a compressed copy into memory, giving the fast, click-through interactivity an executive meeting needs.

questions.q: What shape do the relationships between dw.FactProductSales and its four dimensions take in the Power BI model?
options: Many-to-many in every case
One-to-many, filtering from each dimension (the "one" side) to the fact table (the "many" side)
One-to-one, since each dimension has a unique key
No relationships are needed since the tables are pre-joined in the warehouse
questions.explain: This is the standard star-schema shape: each dimension's surrogate key filters down to the many matching rows in the fact table.

questions.q: Why does dw.DimDate need to be explicitly marked as the model's date table?
options: It's a cosmetic setting with no functional effect
Power BI's time-intelligence DAX functions (like DATEADD) can silently produce wrong results against a date column that was never marked as the official date table
It's required before any relationships can be created at all
Marking it is only needed if the model uses DirectQuery
questions.explain: Marking FullDate as the date column is what lets Power BI's time-intelligence functions treat dw.DimDate as a real calendar instead of just another table.

questions.q: Why does this model deliberately NOT import dw.DimSalesReason or dw.BridgeOrderSalesReason from Lesson 7?
options: Because they were deleted from the warehouse after Chapter 2
Because this dashboard answers "how much and where," not "why," and importing a bridge table adds real fan-out risk with no reporting benefit here
Because Power BI cannot import tables with composite primary keys
Because bridge tables are never allowed in any Power BI model
questions.explain: The Executive Summary and Regional Drill-Down pages never need to slice by sales reason, so leaving the bridge table out avoids an unnecessary fan-out risk.

questions.q: Which five tables does this Power BI model import from the warehouse?
options: dw.FactProductSales, dw.DimProduct, dw.DimDate, dw.DimTerritory, dw.DimCustomer
dw.FactProductSales, dw.DimSalesReason, dw.BridgeOrderSalesReason, dw.DimProduct, dw.DimDate
Only dw.FactProductSales and dw.DimProduct
All dw.* tables plus every stg.* staging table
questions.explain: The model imports exactly the fact table and the four dimensions this capstone's star schema defines — nothing from the sales-reason bridge, and nothing from staging.
